clue.text: Gradually reversing major components of animal selfies?

indicators.note: the major components are the two big words of the answer, each to be read backwards, leaving the small middle word alone

parts.note: pets by pets: photos of household animals taken by the animals themselves

explanation.surface: A question about making animal selfies a little at a time, by reversing their main parts.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer backwards word by word: each STEP turned round is PETS, so STEP BY STEP becomes PETS BY PETS, pets photographed by pets, which is a selfie.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom meaning one stage at a time, so slowly and by degrees.

clue.text: Fun run tops scrubbed, picked up without issue, not tumble-dried

indicators.note: the trimmed words pick up, taking into their middle, the abbreviation that follows
the tops, the first letters, of both words are scrubbed away

parts.note: the two words of the clue, before their first letters go
SP is the abbreviation of Latin sine prole, without issue (no children), used in family trees

explanation.surface: Kit from a charity fun run, tops scrubbed and collected, comes through the wash fine without a spin in the dryer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without issue' looks like 'without trouble' but is the genealogists' s.p., meaning childless.
explanation.definitionFit: Laundry that has not been through a spin cycle or tumble dryer has not been spun.

clue.text: Gathering fool put silver in most of symbol…

indicators.note: silver is put in, placed inside, the shortened symbol word
all but the last letter of the symbol word is used

parts.note: AG is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A meeting in which a fool slips silver into most of a symbol, leading into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: An assemblage is a collection or gathering of people or things.

clue.text: …a symbol head of League displayed before ordinary game

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: Go is the Japanese board game

explanation.surface: Continuing from the previous clue: a league's badge is shown before an everyday match.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipses link it to 3 Down, whose 'symbol' carries on into this clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A logo is an emblem or design used as an organisation's identifying mark.

clue.text: Furtive and diffident about drink with officer

indicators.note: the shy word goes round the other letters

parts.note: LT is the abbreviation for lieutenant, an officer

explanation.surface: A sneaky, timid person is having a drink with an officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealthy and furtive are synonyms, both describing secret, sly behaviour.

clue.text: Kind? There's a limit to sentiment

indicators.note: a limit of a word is one of its two end letters, so asked to name one you might answer with either

parts.note: the word whose end letters are S and T

explanation.surface: A remark that even kindness has to stop somewhere when feelings run high.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'S OR T' as one word: either of the end letters of 'sentiment' is a limit of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sort is a kind or type, as in 'that sort of thing'.

clue.text: Who'll take a position on river?

definitions.text: Who'll take a position on river?

parts.words: Who'll take a position on river?
parts.note: someone who sets up on a riverbank to fish; the clue also hints at a position word followed by R for river

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a question about a military or political stance; it is a fisherman settling on the bank.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who fishes with rod and line takes a spot by the water to catch fish.

clue.text: Insist son should reside in Bury (though not very much)

indicators.note: the son letter lives inside the burying phrase

parts.note: to bury something only a little is to put it one foot down, a single foot deep

explanation.surface: Insisting that a son should go to live in the town of Bury, though not for long.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury looks like the Lancashire town; here it is the verb, and the bracket says the burial is shallow. The S goes after ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: To put your foot down is an idiom for being firm and insisting on something.

clue.text: Supporter of corresponding job a lot of people cut

indicators.note: the last letter is cut off

parts.note: many means a lot of people

explanation.surface: Someone backing a matching job that cost many people their work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corresponding' reads as 'matching'; here it means writing letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The person who delivers the mail keeps letter-writing going, so supports correspondence.

clue.text: Sample I put in further comments for review

indicators.note: a review looks back, so the letters are read backwards
the letter I is placed inside the postscript abbreviation

parts.note: PS, postscript, is a further comment added at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: A sample: I add extra comments for a review.
explanation.definitionFit: To sip is to taste a small amount, so to sample a drink.

clue.text: One used to fly about, sorting out cradle and potty

indicators.note: sorting out rearranges the letters of the two words that follow

explanation.surface: A parent once sorting out the baby's cradle and potty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' belongs to the definition: the creature used to fly about.
explanation.definitionFit: A pterodactyl was a prehistoric flying reptile, extinct now, hence 'used to'.

clue.text: Could possibly be American native, originally

definitions.text: Could possibly be American native, originally

indicators.note: originally means the first letter

explanation.surface: Someone guessing that a figure might be a Native American.
explanation.definitionFit: The Maya are an indigenous people of Central America, so one of them is an American native.

clue.text: One making outcry about closure of derelict part of church?

indicators.note: the shouter goes round the single letter

parts.note: a bellower is someone who shouts loudly

indicators.note: the closure of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone protesting loudly about the closing of a run-down church.
explanation.definitionFit: A bell tower is the part of a church building where the bells hang, a belfry.

clue.text: Bishop, in effect, is in possession of genuine, upstanding crook?

indicators.note: the reversed genuine word holds the rest
in a down clue, standing up means the word reads from bottom to top
the bishop letter goes inside the effect word

parts.note: to wreak is to effect, bring about (wreak havoc)
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop who is in fact holding a genuine, honest crook, his pastoral staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in effect' and 'upstanding' read as 'in fact' and 'honourable'; effect here is the verb wreak, as in wreak havoc, and 'crook' is not the bishop's staff but a criminal.
explanation.definitionFit: A crook is a criminal, someone who breaks the law.

clue.text: We certainly will keep that place in a state of watchfulness

indicators.note: the yes word keeps, holds, the place word inside

explanation.surface: We will definitely guard that spot while staying alert.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping a weather eye open is an idiom for staying alert and watchful.

clue.text: Name remains used in nationalist area

indicators.note: the remains word is used inside the other letters

parts.note: ash is what remains after burning

explanation.surface: A name is being given to remains held in a nationalist region.
explanation.definitionFit: Natasha is a girl's first name, the Russian pet form of Natalia.

clue.text: Left inside shooting Oscar winners essentially with few crew members

indicators.note: the left letter goes inside the shooting word

parts.note: Oscar is the NATO alphabet word for O

indicators.note: the essence is the middle letter

explanation.surface: Shooting a film of Oscar winners with only a small crew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oscar winners' suggests film awards; Oscar is just the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: A skeleton crew or staff is the bare minimum number of people needed.

clue.text: Not regular district hospital room

parts.note: a way can mean a district or neighbourhood, as in 'out our way'
a ward is a room in a hospital

explanation.surface: An irregular hospital room in a district.
explanation.definitionFit: Wayward means unpredictable and erratic, not following a regular or steady course.

clue.text: Measure of volume in alarm curtailed after start of month?

indicators.note: the shortened alarm comes after the date

parts.note: the first of December can be written DEC I, a whimsical way of saying the start of a month

indicators.note: the tail, the last letter, is cut off

explanation.surface: How loud an alarm is, cut short soon after the start of the month.
explanation.walkthrough: The query flags that the 'start of month' is a date, 1 December, written with a Roman I.
explanation.definitionFit: A decibel is the unit used to measure loudness, which is volume of sound.

clue.text: Nobleman keeping up with favourite show producer

indicators.note: the nobleman holds the other letters inside

explanation.surface: A nobleman keeps up with the producer of a show he likes.
explanation.definitionFit: A puppeteer stages and works a puppet show, so produces that kind of performance.

clue.text: Pressure on current measures to secure a region of South America

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure

indicators.note: the amps word secures, holds, the letter A

explanation.surface: Pressure applied to electrical current, as if an engineer were trying to control a South American area.
explanation.definitionFit: The pampas are the vast grassy plains of Argentina and Uruguay.

clue.text: Attitude to morals and other things limiting greeting

indicators.note: the etc letters go round the greeting, limiting it on both sides

parts.note: etc. is short for et cetera, and other things

explanation.surface: An attitude to morals and other matters that limits how one says hello.
explanation.definitionFit: An ethic is a set of moral principles, a stance on what is right.

clue.text: Last target certain to be topped

parts.note: an end is a target or aim

indicators.note: in a down clue, the top letter of the word is removed

explanation.surface: A final target that is sure to be beaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last' looks like an adjective, final; it is the verb meaning to keep going.
explanation.definitionFit: To last and to endure both mean to continue or survive over time.

clue.text: Possibly sow hint of discord in various circuits?

parts.note: a sow is a female pig, which might be a mother boar; possibly flags the jokey description

indicators.note: a hint is just the first letter

explanation.surface: Perhaps a sow is causing a touch of discord at various places.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sow' looks like the verb to plant seeds; it is the female pig.
explanation.definitionFit: A motherboard is the main circuit board of a computer, carrying its many circuits.

clue.text: Carry on with the evidence initially after start of trial

indicators.note: the trial letter comes before the initials, so they are after it
the start of a word is its first letter
take the first letter of each of the next three words

explanation.surface: Proceed with the evidence first, right after the trial opens.
explanation.definitionFit: To tote is to carry, especially something heavy or a weapon.

clue.text: John pens line in observations shared widely

indicators.note: pens means encloses, so the toilet word holds the line letter

parts.note: john and bog are both slang for a toilet

explanation.surface: John writes a line in the notes that everyone sees.
explanation.walkthrough: John looks like a man writing; it is US slang for a lavatory, and bog is the British slang for the same thing.
explanation.definitionFit: A blog is an online journal whose thoughts and remarks are published for everyone to read.

clue.text: It adds strength to ridicule

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a structural ... reinforces a vault, boat or knitted edge
second meaning: to tease or mock them

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one idea, something that strengthens mockery; 'to' just links two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a stiffening support in a structure and a verb for teasing.

clue.text: Scientist negotiated a starry moon role?

indicators.note: negotiated in the sense of worked around, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A scientist discussing a part in a show about a starry moon.
explanation.definitionFit: The Astronomer Royal is the honorary post of Britain's senior astronomer, an eminent scientist.
